source_text: Καὶ τὸ μὲν τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς τόξον ηὐτρέπισεν ὁ πολέμιος· ἀφεῖναι δὲ τὸ βέλος κεκώλυται· μᾶλλον δὲ ἀφῆκε μὲν, ἀντ έστραπται δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ κεφαλήν. Αὐτὸς ἀπολαύει τῶν πικρῶν ἐκείνων δακρύων, ἅπερ ἡμῖν παρεσκεύασεν. Ἀλλὰ ποιήσωμεν, ἀδελφοὶ, τὸ τραῦμα τῷ δυσμενεῖ φορτικώτερον, ἐπιτείνωμεν τὸ πένθος αὐ τοῦ. Τὸ δὲ ὅπως, λέξω μὲν ἐγὼ, πράξατε δὲ ὑμεῖς. Εἰσί τινες ἐκ τῆς ἐπικρατείας τοῦ πυρὸς ἀναρπασθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ κτίσαντος, καὶ μηδεμίαν ἔχοντες περιλελειμμένην αὐτοῖς βίου λοιπὸν ἀφορμὴν, ἀλλὰ μόνῃ τῇ ψυχῇ καὶ τῷ σώματι διαφυγόντες τὸν κίν δυνον. Ἡμεῖς τοίνυν ὅσοι τῆς τῶν δυσχερῶν ἄγευστοι πείρας ἐμείναμεν, κοινὴν ἐκείνοις προθῶμεν τὴν εὐπορίαν τὴν ἑαυτῶν. Ἐναγκαλισώμεθα τοὺς περισωθέντας μόλις τῶν ἀδελφῶν, εἴπωμεν πρὸς ἕκαστον ἕκαστος· Νεκρὸς ἦν, καὶ ἀνέζησεν· ἀπολωλὼς, καὶ εὑρέθη· καὶ τὸ συγγενὲς σῶμα σκεπάσωμεν. Ἀντιστήσωμεν ταῖς τοῦ δυσμενοῦς ἐπηρείαις τὴν ἡμετέραν παράκλησιν, ἵνα καὶ βλάπτων ἐκεῖνος μηδὲν μέγα βλάψαι δοκῇ, καὶ πολεμήσας, μηδένα δεῖξαι νενικημένον, καὶ περιελὼν τὴν εὐπορίαν τῶν ἀδελφῶν, ὑπὸ τῆς ἡμετέρας φιλοτιμίας φανείη νικώ μενος. Ὑμεῖς δὲ οἱ διαφυγόντες τὸν κίνδυνον, ἀδελφοὶ, μὴ σφόδρα ἄχθεσθε τοῖς συμβεβηκόσι κακοῖς, μηδὲ κατασεισθῆτε τὴν ἔννοιαν, ἀλλ' ἀποτινάξασθε τὴν τῆς λύπης ἀχλὺν, καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἀναῤῥώσατε λογι σμοῖς ἀνδρειοτέροις χρησάμενοι, καὶ τὸ συμβεβηκὸς στεφάνων ποιήσασθε πρόφασιν. Ἂν γὰρ ἀκατάσειστοι μείνητε, καὶ τῇ πίστει φανήσεσθε δοκιμώτεροι, καθάπερ χρυσὸς εὐγενὴς ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς ἀναλάμψαντες, καὶ τῷ δυσμενεῖ τὴν αἰσχύνην αὐξήσετε μᾶλλον, ὡς οὐδὲ δάκρυον ὑμῖν δυνηθέντι κινῆσαι, δι' ὧν ἐπεβούλευσεν. Ἀναμνήσατε τῆς τοῦ Ἰὼβ ἑαυτοὺς καρτερίας. Εἴπατε πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς ἅπερ ἐκεῖνος· Ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν, ὁ Κύριος ἀφείλετο· ὡς τῷ Κυ ρίῳ ἔδοξεν, οὕτω καὶ ἐγένετο. Καὶ μηδεὶς ἐξ ὧν ἔπαθεν ἀναπεισθῇ λογίσασθαί τε καὶ λέγειν, ὡς ἄρα οὐδεμία πρόνοια τάττει τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς, μηδὲ κατηγορείτω τῆς οἰκονομίας τοῦ Δεσπότου καὶ κρίσεως· ἀλλ' εἰς τὸν ἀθλητὴν ἐκεῖνον ὁράτω, κἀκεῖνον σύμ βουλον ποιείσθω τοῦ κρείττονος. Ἀναλογιζέσθω τοὺς ἀγῶνας ἅπαντας ἐφεξῆς, ἐφ' οἷς ἐκεῖνος ἠρίστευσε· καὶ πόσοις βέλεσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου βληθεὶς, οὐκ ἐδέξατο καιρίαν πληγήν. Περιεῖλε μὲν γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὴν εὐπραγίαν τῶν οἰκείων, καταχῶσαι δὲ αὐτὸν ταῖς ἐπαλλήλοις τῶν κακῶν ἐβουλεύσατο φήμαις. Ἔτι γὰρ τοῦ προτέρου τὴν τοιάνδε συμφορὰν ἐξαγγέλ λοντος, ἕτερος ἄγγελος ἤρχετο, χειρόνων πραγμά των φέρων κατήφειαν· ἀλλήλοις τε ἐπισυνήπτετο τὰ δεινὰ, καὶ τὴν τῶν κυμάτων ἐπιδρομὴν ἐζήλουν αἱ συμφοραὶ, καὶ πρὶν ἢ παυθῆναι τὸ πρότερον δά κρυον, ἑτέρου προσήγετο πρόφασις. Ὁ δίκαιος δὲ ὥσπερ τις πρόβολος εἱστήκει, τὰς τοῦ χειμῶνος ὑποδεχόμενος προσβολὰς, καὶ ἀλλοιῶν εἰς ἀφρὸν τῶν κυμάτων τὴν βίαν, καὶ τὴν εὐγνώμονα πρὸς τὸν Δεσπότην ἠφίει φωνήν· Ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν, ὁ Κύριος ἀφείλετο· ὡς τῷ Κυρίῳ ἔδοξεν, οὕτω καὶ ἐγένετο· καὶ οὐδὲν τῶν συμβαινόντων δακρύων ἠξίωσεν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἧκέ τις ἀγγέλλων, ὡς τοῖς παισὶ καὶ ταῖς θυγατράσιν εὐωχουμένοις ἐπετίναξε πνεῦμά τι βίαιον τὸ τῆς εὐφροσύνης δωμάτιον, τότε μό νον τὴν ἐσθῆτα διέῤῥηξε, τὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐπιδεικνύμενος συμπαθὲς, καὶ ὅτι πατὴρ εἴη φιλόστορ γος οἷς ἔπραττε μαρτυρόμενος.
thought_title: Turning the devil's arrows back and imitating Job's endurance
orientation: Basil is addressing his congregation after the recent fire, urging them to comfort the survivors and to imitate Job's patient endurance of loss.
pass_a_gloss: And the bow of the plot the enemy prepared; but to release the arrow he has been prevented; or rather he released it, but it has been turned back upon his own head. He himself enjoys those bitter tears which he prepared for us. But let us make, brothers, the wound more burdensome to the hostile one, let us increase his grief. And the how, I will say, but you do it. There are some who from the dominion of the fire were snatched away by the Creator, and have no remaining means of life left to them, but with only the soul and the body escaped the danger. We therefore, as many as have remained without taste of the trial of hardships, let us set before them our own abundance as common. Let us embrace the brothers who were barely saved, let us say each one to each: He was dead, and came to life again; he was lost, and was found; and let us cover the kindred body. Let us oppose to the hostile one's insults our comfort, so that even when harming he may seem to have harmed nothing great, and having waged war, to have shown no one defeated, and having stripped the abundance of the brothers, he may be shown defeated by our generosity. But you who escaped the danger, brothers, do not be excessively grieved at the evils that have happened, nor be shaken in your mind, but shake off the mist of grief, and strengthen your souls using more courageous reasonings, and make what has happened an occasion for crowns. For if you remain unshaken, you will appear more approved in faith, just as noble gold shining forth from the fire, and you will increase the shame of the hostile one rather, as he was not able to move even a tear from you, through the things by which he plotted. Remind yourselves of the endurance of Job. Say to yourselves the very things which he said: The Lord gave, the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so also it happened. And let no one from what he suffered be persuaded to reckon and to say that no providence orders our affairs, nor let him accuse the stewardship of the Master and his judgment; but let him look to that athlete, and let him make him an adviser of the better course. Let him reckon up all the contests in order, in which that man excelled; and by how many arrows struck by the devil, he did not receive a fatal wound. For he stripped away his prosperity of his household, but to bury him with the successive reports of evils he planned. For while the former was still announcing such a calamity, another messenger was coming, bearing the gloom of worse things; and the terrors were joined to one another, and the calamities rivaled the onrush of waves, and before the former tear had ceased, an occasion for another was brought forward. But the righteous man stood like some breakwater, receiving the assaults of the storm, and turning the force of the waves into foam, and he sent forth the grateful voice to the Master: The Lord gave, the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so also it happened; and he deemed none of the things that happened worthy of tears. But when someone came announcing that upon his sons and daughters feasting a violent wind shook the chamber of gladness, then only he tore his garment, showing the sympathy of nature, and testifying by what he did that he was a loving father.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of the enemy as archer preparing a bow, matching the military imagery of the passage.

choices.term: ἀντέστραπται δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ κεφαλήν
choices.english: it has been turned back upon his own head
choices.why: Preserves the perfect tense and the reflexive force of the arrow returning on the shooter.
rejected: it was turned back on his own head
it has recoiled upon his own head

choices.why: The verb means to take into one's arms; 'embrace' captures the physical warmth Basil urges toward the survivors.
The image is of a projecting structure that receives and breaks the force of waves; 'breakwater' fits the storm metaphor that follows.

choices.term: τὴν εὐγνώμονα πρὸς τὸν Δεσπότην ἠφίει φωνήν
choices.english: he sent forth the grateful voice to the Master
choices.why: εὐγνώμων here means rightly disposed or grateful; 'grateful voice' captures Job's thankful submission to God.
δωμάτιον is a small room or chamber; the phrase is vivid and concrete, so 'chamber of gladness' keeps the image.

pass_b_english: The enemy prepared the bow of his plot, but he was prevented from releasing the arrow. Or rather, he did release it, but it has been turned back upon his own head. He himself now tastes those bitter tears he had prepared for us. So let us, brothers and sisters, make the wound heavier for the hostile one; let us increase his grief. How this is to be done, I will tell you, and you will carry it out. There are some who were snatched away from the fire's power by the Creator, and who have no remaining means of livelihood left to them, but escaped the danger with only soul and body. Let all of us, then, who have remained untouched by the experience of hardships, set before them our own abundance as a common store. Let us embrace the brothers and sisters who barely survived, and let each of us say to each of them: 'He was dead, and has come back to life; he was lost, and has been found' (Luke 15:24). And let us cover the body that belongs to our own kin. Let us oppose the hostile one's assaults with our own consolation, so that even when he harms us he may seem to have harmed nothing great, and when he makes war he may show no one defeated, and when he strips away the abundance of our brothers and sisters he may be shown defeated by our generosity.

But you who escaped the danger, brothers and sisters, do not be overly distressed by the evils that have happened, and do not let your minds be shaken. Instead, shake off the mist of grief and strengthen your souls with more courageous reasoning, and make what has happened an occasion for crowns. For if you remain unshaken, you will be shown more approved in faith, shining forth from the fire like noble gold, and you will increase the shame of the hostile one all the more, since he could not move even a tear from you through the things he plotted. Remind yourselves of Job's endurance. Say to yourselves what he said: 'The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it has happened' (Job 1:21). And let no one be persuaded by what he has suffered to reason and say that no providence orders our affairs, and let no one accuse the stewardship and judgment of the Master. Instead, let him look to that athlete and make him his counselor toward what is better. Let him reckon up all the contests in order, in which that man excelled, and how many arrows he was struck with by the devil without receiving a mortal wound. For the devil stripped away his prosperity in his household, but he planned to bury him under the successive reports of evils. For while the first messenger was still announcing one disaster, another messenger came, bringing the gloom of worse events. The terrors were joined one to another, and the disasters rivaled the onrush of waves; before the first tear had ceased, the occasion for another was brought forward. But the righteous man stood like a breakwater, receiving the assaults of the storm, turning the force of the waves into foam, and he sent forth the grateful voice to the Master: 'The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it has happened' (Job 1:21). And he considered none of the things that happened worthy of tears. But when someone came announcing that a violent wind had struck the chamber of gladness while his sons and daughters were feasting, then alone he tore his garment, showing the sympathy of nature and testifying by what he did that he was a tenderly loving father.

last_rejected.why: 'Sympathy of nature' is misleading; συμπαθὲς here means natural affection/compassion, not 'sympathy of nature' as a philosophical concept.
last_rejected.fix: showing the compassion natural to our humanity
last_rejected.ruling: συμπαθὲς means natural fellow-feeling; 'sympathy of nature' is awkward but within range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: and let each of us say to each of them: 'He was dead, and has come back to life; he was lost, and has been found'
last_rejected.source_quote: εἴπωμεν πρὸς ἕκαστον ἕκαστος· Νεκρὸς ἦν, καὶ ἀνέζησεν· ἀπολωλὼς, καὶ εὑρέθη
last_rejected.why: English adds 'to each of them' making it individual address; Greek ἕκαστος is nominative 'let each one say,' not 'to each of them.' The dative would be ἑκάστῳ. This changes the structure: each survivor is addressed by each helper, but 'to each of them' over-specifies.
last_rejected.fix: let each of us say: 'He was dead, and has come back to life; he was lost, and has been found'
last_rejected.ruling: πρὸς ἕκαστον ἕκαστος = 'each to each'; 'to each of them' fairly renders the reciprocal address, not a major change.

last_rejected.quote: he may seem to have harmed nothing great
last_rejected.why: Greek means 'he may seem to have accomplished no great harm' or 'to have harmed nothing of importance,' but English 'harmed nothing great' is awkward and slightly misleading—'nothing of importance' or 'no great harm' is clearer.
last_rejected.fix: he may seem to have done no great harm
last_rejected.ruling: μηδὲν μέγα βλάψαι = 'harm nothing great'; English is awkward but accurate, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: and testifying by what he did that he was a tenderly loving father
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ὅτι πατὴρ εἴη φιλόστοργος οἷς ἔπραττε μαρτυρόμενος
last_rejected.why: English omits the crucial concessive/optative force: εἴη is 'that he was' (indirect statement after ἐπιδεικνύμενος), but οἷς ἔπραττε 'by what he did'—the Greek emphasizes he proved by his actions that he was a loving father. English 'testifying by what he did' captures this. Actually checking: 'οἷς ἔπραττε μαρτυρόμενος' = 'testifying by what he did.' This seems correct.
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly renders εἴη φιλόστοργος οἷς ἔπραττε μαρτυρόμενος; no omission or error present.
